fi-chaetodon-auriga.title: Auriga Butterflyfish
fi-chaetodon-auriga.summary: Also called the Threadfin Butterflyfish. One of the hardier butterflyfish, but not for reef tanks.
rows: About 8 in; wild record 25 cm (9.8 in) TL (FishBase)
No. Eats coral polyps and other invertebrates
Omnivore. Meaty foods such as mysis, chopped seafood and frozen marine mixes
Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa (extending to Mossel Bay, South Africa, ) to the Hawaiian, Marquesan, and Ducie islands, north to southern Japan
notes: Shy at first; give it several hiding places.
Best in a fish-only tank with live rock.

fi-heniochus-acuminatus.title: Black & White Heniochus
fi-heniochus-acuminatus.summary: A peaceful bannerfish with a long white dorsal streamer and bold black bands.
rows: About 8½ in; wild record 25 cm (9.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Can be kept with its own kind if all are added together
Omnivore. Small meaty foods and herbivore preparations
Indo-Pacific: Persian/Arabian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, Tanzania to South Africa, Madagascar, Seychelles, Mascarenes, St Brandon Shoals, Chagos
notes: Needs a large tank with swimming room.

fi-chelmon-rostratus.title: Copperband Butterflyfish
fi-chelmon-rostratus.summary: A striking butterflyfish with copper bands and a long beak for picking food from crevices. Useful against Aiptasia, but hard to keep.
rows: About 8 in; wild record 20 cm (7.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep singly, not with other copperbands or similar butterflyfish
With caution. May pick at invertebrates, especially anemones and feather dusters
Carnivore. A shy, slow feeder; offer a variety of small meaty foods until it starts eating
Western Pacific: Andaman Sea to Ryukyu Islands and Australia
notes: Best in a large, calm tank without bullies.

fi-chaetodon-xanthurus.title: Pearlscale Butterflyfish
fi-chaetodon-xanthurus.summary: A pearly white butterflyfish with a dark crosshatch pattern. Better in fish-only tanks with live rock.
rows: About 6 in; wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) SL (standard length) (FishBase)
Omnivore. A varied diet of meaty foods
Western Pacific: Indonesia and the Philippines, north to the Ryukyu Islands
notes: Needs 70 gal or more; suited to fish-only tanks with live rock.

fi-chaetodon-lunula.title: Raccoon Butterflyfish
fi-chaetodon-lunula.summary: A yellow-orange butterflyfish with a black "raccoon mask" over the eyes. Peaceful, but for fish-only tanks.
rows: About 8 in; wild record 20 cm (7.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Can live with other butterflyfish in a big tank
Omnivore. Meaty foods, mysis and frozen marine preparations several times a day once settled
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Hawaiian, Marquesan, and Ducie islands, north to southern Japan, south to Lord Howe and Rapa islands
notes: Mostly active at night in the wild, often in pairs.

fi-chaetodon-ephippium.title: Saddleback Butterflyfish
fi-chaetodon-ephippium.summary: A gray butterflyfish with a large black, white-edged saddle at the back and orange on the face.
rows: About 9 in; wild record 30 cm (11.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep one, or a male-female pair
No. Eats most stony corals, some soft corals and live rock invertebrates
Omnivore. A variety of meaty preparations
Indo-Pacific: Sri Lanka and Cocos-Keeling Islands to the Hawaiian, Marquesan and Tuamoto islands, north to southern Japan, south to Rowley Shoals and New South Wales
notes: Needs a large tank (130 gal minimum) with swimming room and good water quality.

fi-forcipiger-flavissimus.title: Yellow Longnose Butterflyfish
fi-forcipiger-flavissimus.summary: A bright yellow butterflyfish with a long, plier-like snout. Also called the Forcepsfish.
rows: About 9 in; wild record 22 cm (8.7 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Small meaty foods it can pick from rock crevices
Indo-Pacific: East Africa and Red Sea to the Hawaiian and Easter islands, north to southern Japan, south to Lord Howe Island; throughout Micronesia
notes: Hardy in a fish-only system once acclimated.

fi-chaetodon-capistratus.title: Four-Eye Butterflyfish
fi-chaetodon-capistratus.summary: A western Atlantic butterflyfish with a big false eyespot near the tail that confuses predators. Pretty but delicate and often hard to get eating.
rows: About 6 in; wild record 15 cm (5.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Singly, or as a male-female pair; same-sex fish may fight

Carnivore that feeds on polyps and worms in the wild. Start with live enriched brine shrimp, clam and minced squid or shrimp, then move to mysis and frozen carnivore foods; feed at least three times a day
Western Atlantic: Massachusetts, USA and Bermuda to West Indies and northern South America
warn: Not for reef tanks: it eats stony coral and gorgonian polyps.

fi-chaetodon-kleinii.title: Klein's Butterflyfish (Sunburst Butterfly)
fi-chaetodon-kleinii.summary: A golden-yellow butterflyfish with a dark bar through the eye, found across the Indo-Pacific. One of the hardier butterflies, but it nips soft corals, so it suits fish-only tanks best.
rows: About 6 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 15 cm (5.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Can be kept singly or as a group if added together to a large tank
Omnivore: frozen mysis, brine shrimp, chopped seafood and quality prepared foods in two or three small meals a day
Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa (south to Coffee Bay, South Africa,) to the Hawaiian Islands and Samoa, north to southern Japan, south to New South Wales
notes: Some individuals eat Aiptasia anemones, but not reliably.
warn: May nip soft corals and small tube-dwelling inverts.

fi-heniochus-monoceros.title: Masked Bannerfish (Masked Heniochus)
fi-heniochus-monoceros.summary: A big white-and-black bannerfish with a yellow rear half, from Indo-Pacific reefs. Peaceful, but it grows large and needs room.
rows: About 9 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 24 cm (9.4 in) TL (FishBase)
Adults often pair in the wild
Omnivore: frozen meaty foods such as mysis, krill and clam, plus some seaweed
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Tuamoto Islands, north to southern Japan, south to New South Wales and Tonga
warn: Watch it in a reef tank: some nip coral polyps.
